content.title: About
content.content: Gin Fizz is a classic cocktail made with gin, fresh lemon juice, simple syrup and carbonated water. It is light, refreshing and features a bright citrus note highlighted by the juniper-forward gin.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink originated in the early 1920s in the United States as a variation of the popular “fizz” style, which mixes spirit with soda.
The original recipe calls for a simple syrup rather than pre‑made sweetened syrup.
Some versions add egg white, creating a frothy texture often called a “Fizz with foam”.
Gin Fizz is typically served in a highball glass, garnished with a lemon wedge or a sprig of rosemary.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: When consumed in moderation, the cocktail is low in calories because the bulk of the drink is carbonated water.

items.title: Vitamin C from lemon
items.content: Fresh lemon juice provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Digestive boost from gin
items.content: Gin, containing juniper berries, may aid digestion and offers a subtle aromatic effect.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Like any alcoholic beverage, Gin Fizz can cause intoxication and is not recommended for pregnant individuals, people with liver disease, or those taking certain medications.

items.title: Lemon acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach of people with gastritis or ulcer disease.

items.title: Gin allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to gin components such as juniper.

content.title: How to Make
content.content: Combine 45 ml gin, 30 ml fresh lemon juice and 15 ml simple syrup in a shaker with ice. Shake well, then strain into a highball glass filled with ice and top with carbonated water. Garnish with a lemon wedge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ingredients separately: gin in a cool, dark place, lemons in the refrigerator, and use carbonated water shortly after opening.
